title: Generic numerical data of a proper component in an ambient nodal family
statement: Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $(Z,M)$ be a multipointed $S$-curve [def-trf-multipointed-curve]. Assume that every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] of $Z/S$ has only ordinary nodes as nonsmooth points: over an algebraically closed residue field $F$, the completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] at a nonsmooth point is $F[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Assume that each $M_s$ is etale over $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and lies in the smooth locus of $Z_s$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $H\hookrightarrow Z$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] over $S$, such that every geometric fibre $H_{\bar s}$ is a reduced irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] of $Z_{\bar s}$. There is a nonempty open $V\subseteq S$ on which the self-nodes of $H_{\bar s}$ and the DISTINCT points of $H_{\bar s}\cap(M_{\bar s}\cup\operatorname{Sing}(Z_{\bar s}))$ are the geometric fibres of finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] etale $V$-schemes. The first set means ambient nodes whose two branches both lie on $H_{\bar s}$; the second is taken with reduced structure and counts each point once. Moreover $p(s)=\dim_{\bar\kappa(s)}H^1(H_{\bar s},\mathcal O)$ [def-sc-zariski-cohomology] is finite and constant for $s\in V$, independently of the algebraic closure. The cardinalities of the two indicated finite sets are also constant on $V$, independently of the algebraic closure. Properness is imposed on $H/S$ only; neither $Z/S$ nor $M/S$ is required to be proper or finite.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34, weighted contracted-component data; agent-extracted single-component numerical spreading lemma. EGA IV3 9.7.9, 9.7.12 and EGA III2 7.6.9 are the cited incidence/cohomology inputs. Properness here belongs to the supplied H, not to the ambient curve.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar s$ with algebraically closed residue field $F$, and put $C=Z_{\bar s}$ and $D=H_{\bar s}$. By [def-trf-multipointed-curve], $Z/S$ is finitely presented and its ordinary fibres have pure dimension one. Apply [lem-trf-relative-dimension-base-change] to the geometric-point base change: $C$ is pure of dimension one, and is finite type over $F$. By [lem-trf-nodal-points-reduced-algebraically-closed], $C$ is reduced. The hypothesis on $H$ says that $D$ is one reduced irreducible component, hence is pure of dimension one. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-subcurve-boundary] with $X=C$, $Y=D$ and $N=C$: $D$ is nodal, and it is smooth at every point where it meets the closure of $C\setminus D$. Away from that closure, $D=C$ on an open neighbourhood: in a reduced affine ring the intersection of the minimal primes is zero, and after removing the other components only the prime defining $D$ remains. Thus the nodes of $D$ are exactly the ambient nodes with both branches on $D$. At a point meeting another component the boundary assertion makes $D$ smooth; at an ambient node meeting no other component the two branches both belong to $D$ and the open-neighbourhood equality makes it a node of $D$. This also covers an irreducible component with a self-node.

source.place: Tag 0E38, lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, statement (1), (2)(c) and proof distinguishing nodes on one component from nodes on two components; reducedness input as in Tag 0E37; geometric fibre dimension: Morphisms Tag 02NK, lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d

proof.text: Write $\Sigma_H=\operatorname{Sing}(H/S)$ and $\Sigma_Z=\operatorname{Sing}(Z/S)$ for the first-Fitting singular subschemes. Step 1 verifies the nodal-fibre hypothesis for $H/S$; its flatness and finite presentation are assumed. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] to $H/S$ and $Z/S$. These singular schemes are closed, commute with every base change, and are unramified over $S$. Set $Q=\Sigma_H$, $P=H\times_Z\Sigma_Z$ and $R=H\times_Z M$. Both $P\to H$ and $R\to H$ are closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. All three schemes $Q,P,R$ are proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], using only properness of $H/S$. Their geometric fibres are respectively the singular subscheme of $H_{\bar s}$, its scheme-theoretic intersection with the ambient singular subscheme, and its scheme-theoretic intersection with the marking. In particular, the first has the desired self-node support by step 1.

source.place: Tags 0C59 and 0C5B, lemma-nodal-family and lemma-base-change-nodal-family; closed immersion base change and properness: Morphisms Tags 01QR and 01W5

proof.text: The morphisms $P/S$ and $R/S$ are also unramified. To check this without assuming either $\Sigma_Z/S$ or $M/S$ proper, work on a geometric fibre over $F$. By [lem-trf-geometric-fibre-unramified-criterion], $(\Sigma_Z)_{\bar s}/F$ is unramified. By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-over-field-discrete] its points are open, and by [lem-trf-unramified-over-field-local-criterion] their local rings are finite separable extensions of $F$, hence are $F$ itself. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $P\to\Sigma_Z$ and $R\to M$ (base changes of $H\to Z$) and their geometric fibres are closed immersions. Its closed subscheme $P_{\bar s}$ therefore consists of a subset of these reduced points: a quotient of the local ring $F$ is either zero or $F$. For $R$, the hypothesis makes $M_s/\kappa(s)$ etale, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] makes $M_{\bar s}/F$ etale. The fibre description [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] expresses it as a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $F$, again just copies of $F$. Its closed subscheme $R_{\bar s}$ likewise selects reduced points. The local-ring criterion just cited makes both $P_{\bar s}/F$ and $R_{\bar s}/F$ unramified. Finally $P/S$ and $R/S$ are locally of finite type, since they are proper by step 2. Apply the converse of [lem-trf-geometric-fibre-unramified-criterion] to obtain their unramifiedness over $S$. This argument includes empty intersections.

source.place: Tags 02G7, 02G8, 02GO and 02GL: unramified-over-field, unramified-etale-fibres, base-change-etale, etale-over-field

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-generic-flat-finite-presentation] separately to $Q/S$, $P/S$ and $R/S$. Its source hypothesis holds because these are proper morphisms, hence locally of finite type and quasi-compact, and $S$ is integral. Intersect the three resulting nonempty opens. Their intersection $U$ is nonempty because $S$ is irreducible. Over $U$ the three maps are flat and locally of finite presentation. Their unramifiedness restricts to $U$ (the diagonal is the restriction of the original open immersion). By [def-weil-etale-morphism] all three maps over $U$ are etale.

source.place: Tag 052A, proposition-generic-flatness, structure-sheaf case; Tag 02GI / 02GV, etale definition and flat-unramified criterion

proof.text: Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $S$, which lies in $U$. Each of $Q_U,P_U,R_U$ remains proper over $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], its fibre at $\eta$ is discrete. That fibre is proper over $\kappa(\eta)$ by the same proper-base-change statement, so it is quasi-compact; its cover by singleton open subsets therefore has a finite subcover. Its underlying set is finite. Apply [lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near] at $\eta$ to each of the three proper maps, and intersect the resulting neighbourhoods. On the resulting nonempty open $W\subseteq U$, all three maps are finite and etale. Subsequent open restrictions preserve finiteness, since on affine opens a finite algebra stays finite after localization; etaleness is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change].

source.place: Tag 02UP, lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood, applied at the generic point; fibre description: Morphisms Tag 02GL; proper base change: Morphisms Tag 01W4

proof.text: Over $W$ use $Q_W$ for the self-node scheme and $T=P_W\amalg R_W$ for the incidence scheme. The latter is finite and etale: over any affine open of $W$ its algebra is the product of the two finite algebras for $P_W$ and $R_W$, generated by the union of their finite module generating sets; etaleness holds on its two open summands. For each geometric fibre, the supports of $P_{\bar s}$ and $R_{\bar s}$ are disjoint. By hypothesis $M_s$ lies in an open $U_s\subseteq Z_s$ smooth over $\kappa(s)$; by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], clause (2), its base change $U_{\bar s}\subseteq Z_{\bar s}$ is smooth over $F$ and contains $M_{\bar s}$. By [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] the underlying set of $(\Sigma_Z)_{\bar s}$ is the nonsmooth locus of $Z_{\bar s}$, which misses $U_{\bar s}$; so $R_{\bar s}\subseteq M_{\bar s}$ and $P_{\bar s}\subseteq(\Sigma_Z)_{\bar s}$ have disjoint supports. The closed immersion into $H_{\bar s}$ is injective on points on each summand. Step 3 shows that these fibres have reduced structure. Consequently the geometric fibre of $T$ identifies with the DISTINCT points of $H_{\bar s}\cap(M_{\bar s}\cup\operatorname{Sing}(Z_{\bar s}))$, with each point occurring once. This construction requires no finiteness of the ambient marking.

source.place: Agent combination of the two disjoint special-point loci, using the marking-in-the-smooth-locus hypothesis; finite-product algebra calculation and etale locality on the two summands

proof.text: Apply [thm-pc-semicontinuity-base-change], parts (1) and (2), to $H/S$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_H$, and $q=1$. The morphism is proper and of finite presentation by hypothesis. The structure sheaf is finitely presented as an $\mathcal O_H$-module (free of rank one), and is flat over $S$ by flatness of $H/S$. Thus $\beta(s)=\dim_{\kappa(s)}H^1(H_s,\mathcal O_{H_s})$ is a finite natural number and is upper semicontinuous. On the nonempty open $W$, choose the least attained value $b$ of $\beta$. The set $V=\{s\in W:\beta(s)<b+1\}$ is nonempty and open in $S$, and $\beta=b$ there by minimality of $b$. For any $s$ and any algebraic closure $F$ of $\kappa(s)$, $H_s$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and a field extension is flat (a vector space is free). Apply [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent] to obtain $H^1(H_{\bar s},\mathcal O)\cong H^1(H_s,\mathcal O)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}F$. A basis of the finite-dimensional vector space on the right before extension remains a basis after tensoring. Therefore $p(s)=\beta(s)$, for every choice of algebraic closure. In particular $p=b$ on $V$.

source.place: Tag 0BDN, lemma-jump-loci-geometric, finiteness and upper semicontinuity; coherent.tex Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, field-extension case

proof.text: Restrict $Q_W$ and $T$ to the nonempty open $V$ of step 7. They are finite etale by steps 5 and 6. Since $V$ is a nonempty open of an integral scheme, it is irreducible and connected. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-degree], parts (a) and (b), separately to these two finite etale maps: there are integers $a,c\geq0$ such that every geometric fibre has respectively $a$ and $c$ reduced points, independently of the algebraically closed field representing the geometric point. Steps 1, 2 and 6 identify these fibres with exactly the self-nodes and the distinct incidence points requested. Together with step 7 this proves all assertions. Empty singular or marking intersections correspond to degree zero; no properness or finiteness of $Z/S$ or $M/S$ was used.

Supplies the reduced point description of the marking fibres and discrete generic fibres of the three etale maps.
Makes the three proper unramified maps flat and locally finitely presented on a common nonempty open.

Clause (2) only: smoothness of the open containing M_s survives base change to the geometric fibre, giving disjointness of marking and ambient singular incidences; the unit has no smooth base-change node.
